questions.enonce_markdown: **(i)** The heights of students in an institution are normally distributed with mean 156 cm and standard deviation 5 cm. Find the probability that a student selected at random has a height between 154 cm and 163 cm.

**(ii)** A packet contains a large number of seeds, 40% of which are advertised to give red flowers. 500 plants are produced out of the seeds from the packet.

(a) Find the mean and variance of the number of plants having red flowers amongst the 500 produced.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of red-flowered plants among $500$: $X \sim B(n = 500,\ p = 0.4)$, $q = 1 - p = 0.6$.

$$E(X) = np = 500 \times 0.4 = 200, \qquad \operatorname{Var}(X) = npq = 500 \times 0.4 \times 0.6 = 120$$

**Mean $= 200$ and variance $= 120$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the normal distribution as an approximation to the binomial distribution, find the probability that of the 500 plants produced,

(b) more than 190 will have red flowers.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $np = 200$ and $nq = 300$ are both large, $X \sim B(500, 0.4)$ is approximated by $Y \sim N(200,\ 120)$, $\sigma = \sqrt{120} = 10.954$.

"More than 190" means $X \ge 191$; with the continuity correction this is $Y > 190.5$.

$$z = \frac{190.5 - 200}{10.954} = -0.867$$

$$P(X > 190) \approx P(Z > -0.867) = \Phi(0.867) = 0.807$$

**$P(\text{more than } 190) \approx 0.807$** (with $z$ rounded to $-0.87$ in tables: $0.8078$).
themes: normal approximation to the binomial distribution

questions.corrige_markdown:
With the continuity correction, "exactly $220$" becomes $219.5 < Y < 220.5$:

$$z_1 = \frac{219.5 - 200}{10.954} = 1.780, \qquad z_2 = \frac{220.5 - 200}{10.954} = 1.871$$

$$P(X = 220) \approx \Phi(1.871) - \Phi(1.780) = 0.9693 - 0.9625 = 0.0068\ldots$$

**$P(\text{exactly } 220) \approx 0.007$** (more precisely $0.0069$ from the unrounded values; the exact binomial value is $0.00690$).
themes: normal approximation to the binomial distribution
